newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe's Mugabe, top aides double their salaries.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe's Mugabe, top aides double their salaries.

text.p: Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe and his senior government aides have more than doubled their salaries and allowances with effect from July, the state news agency ZIANA reported on Friday.
It said Mugabe, his two vice-presidents, cabinet ministers and members of parliament would get twice their current earnings, with the president's total annual takings rising to Z$456,000 ($44,700).
Zimbabwean civil servants crippled key social services for a fortnight when they went on strike on August 20, demanding wage rises of between 30 percent and 60 percent.
They had rejected as an insult an up to nine percent award they had been given, saying it was inadequate in the face of high annual inflation that has averaged 22 percent in the last two years.

Mugabe's cash-strapped government eventually persuaded the strikers -- who included doctors, nurses, magistrates, prosecutors and mortuary attendants -- back to work with a 20 percent increment in addition to the up to nine percent and open-ended talks on salaries and conditions of service. ($1=10.2 Zimbabwe dollars)
